rubric.why: Identifies the increase in atomic size down the group as the relevant condition.
rubric.description: Atomic size increases down the group.
rubric.how: Award for stating that atomic size increases down the group.

rubric.why: Connects weaker attraction to the metals becoming softer and easier to cut.
rubric.description: Weaker interatomic attraction makes the metals softer down the group.
rubric.how: Award for linking weaker interatomic attraction with metals becoming softer.

modelAnswer: Increase in the atomic size down the first group also weakens the interatomic attraction of the atomic metals.
This fact makes them softer down the group and their melting points decrease.

rubric.why: States the relevant trend in the reactivity of Group 1 elements.
rubric.description: Reactivity of Group 1 elements increases down the group.
rubric.how: Award for stating that Group 1 reactivity increases down the group.

rubric.why: Predicts potassium's vigorous reaction with halogens and the product formed.
rubric.description: Potassium reacts vigorously with halogens to form potassium halides.
rubric.how: Award for predicting a vigorous reaction with halogens and potassium halide formation.

modelAnswer: Halogens are very reactive non-metals and react with alkali and alkaline earth metals. The chemical reactivity of the elements in group-1 increases down the group.
Therefore, potassium reacts vigorously with halogens to form potassium halides.

rubric.why: Identifies helium as the noble gas with the lowest boiling point.
rubric.description: Helium has the lowest boiling point.

rubric.why: Gives the reason that helium is the smallest noble gas, consistent with the very low boiling points of noble gases.
rubric.description: Helium is the smallest noble gas; noble gases have very low boiling points.
rubric.how: Award for stating that helium is the smallest noble gas.

modelAnswer: Helium should have the lowest boiling point because noble gases have very low boiling points and helium is the smallest noble gas.

rubric.why: Identifies the increase in atomic size down the group and the greater number of electrons.
rubric.description: Halogen atoms get larger and have more electrons down the group.
rubric.how: Award for stating that the atoms become larger and/or have more electrons down the group.

rubric.why: Links stronger attraction between molecules to iodine's solid state at room temperature.
rubric.description: The molecules attract each other more strongly, so iodine exists as a solid at room temperature.
rubric.how: Award for connecting stronger molecular attraction with iodine being solid at room temperature.

modelAnswer: Atomic radii, melting and boiling points of halogens increase when you go down the group. This is because the atoms get larger as they have more electrons.
As a result the molecules which are formed from these atoms will attract each other with a stronger force.

rubric.why: Gives a physical property that distinguishes transition elements in the textbook answer.
rubric.description: Transition elements are often hard, dense, have high melting and boiling points, or are malleable and ductile.
rubric.how: Award for any one stated physical property from the answer.

rubric.why: Identifies characteristic chemical or compound properties of transition elements.
rubric.description: Transition elements show variable oxidation states and form often-coloured compounds.
rubric.how: Award for stating variable oxidation states or that their compounds are often coloured.

modelAnswer: Transition elements are often hard with higher densities. Their melting and boiling points are also high. These metals show variable oxidation states and the compounds they form are often coloured.

rubric.why: Explains that the converter changes harmful exhaust gases into gases that do not pollute the atmosphere.
rubric.description: A catalytic converter converts harmful gases from the engine into gases that do not pollute the atmosphere.
rubric.how: Award for describing the conversion of harmful exhaust gases into less harmful or non-polluting gases.

rubric.why: Names the catalysts specified in the textbook answer.
rubric.description: The catalysts used are platinum, palladium and rhodium.
rubric.how: Award for naming all three catalysts: platinum, palladium and rhodium.

modelAnswer: A catalytic converter is a device used in the exhaust of an automobile which converts more harmful gases produced in the engine to such gases which do not pollute the atmosphere.
Platinum, palladium and rhodium are the catalysts used in catalytic converters.
